questions.question: A child process must be able to declare its own stop window, in seconds, in its process config, and the orchestrator config must be able to cap such windows with a ceiling. The window value travels as-is (any type) from the recipe blueprint schema to the launch dictionary and is judged only later: a valid window is a finite number above zero and not a boolean. Which two schema classes get the new optional field, which module holds the two string constants that name the per-child key and the ceiling key, and which function in that module decides whether such a value is valid?
questions.note: class=described. Derived from b1e695121 (lifecycle-stop-ownership Task 1.11). git show b1e695121: new typed field stop_window_s in ProcessConfig and ProcessLaunchConfig (Annotated field, declaration spans ~9 lines), new constants STOP_WINDOW_KEY and MAX_STOP_WINDOW_KEY, new function valid_window_s in stop_budget.py. Weak spots: the two constants are on adjacent lines so their +-3 windows overlap; the registry/spawner/PM sites of the same commit (ProcessRegistry, ProcessSpawner.stop, the PM budget code) are not in the reference, the question asks only for the config surface.

questions.question: In the robot v2 driver the 'park' sequence (go home, then servo off) runs its home move as a background program. When the transport drops during that program, the program thread notices the error before the periodic tick guard does, and the sequence ends with the generic 'home move failed' text instead of the 'link to the robot lost' reason. The program thread must report a distinct outcome for transport errors (but not for errors reported by the robot or for compile errors), and the park state machine must map that outcome to the link-lost text. Which method runs the program thread and which park method turns the outcome into the final text?
questions.note: class=described. Derived from 57f4a3dee (robot-protocol-v2 T5.3e.1, A8 flake). git show 57f4a3dee: ProgramMixin._program_loop (link_lost flag, outcome 'link' passed to program_finished) and ParkMachine._advance_locked (outcome == 'link' -> TEXT_PARK_LINK) changed; RobotState.program_finished changed only a comment (not in the reference). Weak spot: both edits are 15-30 lines below the def line the reference points at.

questions.question: The system configuration (system.yaml) must get a new section about closing the system. It holds a list of pre-stop steps whose items are free-form (each step is validated later by the process manager, so a bad step must not reject loading the config), and a bare 'pre_stop:' key with no value must mean an empty list. The root config schema class gets a field for the new section, and the system builder must put the list into the orchestrator config dictionary as an independent deep copy so the process manager can read it. Which new section class, which root-schema field and which builder method?
questions.note: class=described. Derived from f1f904d6e (gui-graceful-close Task 1.4m, merged by 220bd757a). git show f1f904d6e: new class ShutdownSection (field pre_stop, validator), new field SystemConfig.shutdown, one new orchestrator_config entry inside SystemBuilder.build. Weak spots: ShutdownSection is a new class; the edit in SystemBuilder.build is at line 757, ~134 lines below the def line the reference points at; no window covers the changed line.

questions.question: `BackendDriver.system_shutdown` returns outcomes=None. After the shutdown command is accepted it must poll the process manager's supervision status and return the stop outcome of every child, the names without a confirmed outcome and a timed-out flag. Polling ends when every child has an outcome, or the system stop phase is 'done', or the connection is lost. Which method does the polling, and in the MCP tool module which wrapper function must forward an optional wait_timeout to the driver and which module-level registry list holds the tool's description and input schema where that parameter is documented?
questions.note: class=named. Derived from 6fb83337e (gui-graceful-close Task 1.4, driver part). git show 6fb83337e: BackendDriver.system_shutdown rewritten, new helper BackendDriver._poll_shutdown_outcomes, mcp_tools._system_shutdown forwards wait_timeout, the system_shutdown entry of the TOOLS list got a new description and a wait_timeout schema property. Weak spots: the polling helper is new; the TOOLS edit is at line 856, ~310 lines below the declaration line of the list (the reference points at the declaration).

questions.question: `ProcessConfig.as_generic_config` merges typed fields and the extras dict through a nested helper that logs a WARNING when the two values differ. Two distinct NaN float objects (also inside dict, list or tuple values, which happens after the process boundary) compare as different, so a false conflict warning is logged. Which nested function inside `as_generic_config` makes the comparison, and which module-level function must provide an equality in which NaN equals NaN at any depth of dict, list and tuple (while a list and a tuple with the same items still differ)?
questions.note: class=named. Derived from 4caf78912 (lifecycle-stop-ownership C-79). git show 4caf78912: new module-level _same_config_value, one changed comparison line inside the nested _pick of ProcessConfig.as_generic_config. Weak spots: _same_config_value is new; the edited line is ~15 lines below the def of the nested _pick; nested function symbol 'ProcessConfig.as_generic_config._pick' is matched by its last part only.

questions.question: Pipeline-tab Save, the layout autosave and the Recipes-tab Save must not overwrite a recipe file that was changed outside the editor after it was loaded. `TopologySession` remembers the revision the editor was built on, and a method of it returns that remembered revision only when asked for the same recipe slug (None for another slug). `LayoutController` must pass that revision as the expected one in the autosave method and in the manual save-to-active-recipe method and report a conflict (a dialog in Save, a log warning in the autosave); `RecipesPresenter` does the same in its save handler. The message shown to the operator lives in a module-level constant in each of the two modules. Which methods and constants?
questions.note: class=named.
